text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, situated in the
northwest Pacific Ocean. Comprising 6,852 islands, the
country spans four main landmasses—Hokkaido, Honshu,
Shikoku, and Kyushu. With a population of approximately
125 million, Japan is the world's eleventh most populous
country and third-largest economy by nominal GDP.

Japan's unique blend of ancient traditions and cutting-edge innovation makes it one of the world's most fascinating destinations. From the neon-lit streets of Tokyo to the serene temples of Kyoto, from the culinary capital of Osaka to the poignant peace memorials of Hiroshima, the country offers an extraordinary range of experiences. Its efficient rail network, including the iconic Shinkansen bullet trains, connects modern metropolises with pristine natural landscapes—including snow-capped mountains, volcanic hot springs, and lush bamboo forests—making every journey itself a cultural immersion.
Japan maintains the world's third-largest economy
by nominal GDP. After decades of rapid growth in
the post-war era, the economy has experienced periods
of stagnation and recovery. Recent figures reflect
the impact of currency depreciation, as the yen
weakened significantly against the US dollar from

g.text: The dynamic capital: Shibuya Crossing, Meiji Shrine, Senso-ji, Tsukiji Market, Akihabara, and world-class dining.
Ancient capital with 2,000+ temples: Fushimi Inari, Kinkaku-ji, Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, and traditional geisha districts.
Japan's kitchen: Dotonbori street food, Osaka Castle, Universal Studios, takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and vibrant nightlife.
Peace Memorial Park, the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, and resilient spirit of remembrance.
Japan's highest peak (3,776m), onsen hot springs, Lake Ashi cruises, and stunning views of the iconic volcanic cone.
Northern wilderness: powder snow skiing in Niseko, Furano lavender fields, Sapporo beer, fresh seafood, and national parks.

text.tspan: Sources and Notes: GDP data from World Bank Open Data and IMF World Economic Outlook (nominal, current US$). Population figures from Statistics Bureau of Japan and Ministry of Justice (2023 est.). City populations refer to metro area estimates.
